abstract: Building on the unconditional Montgomery pair-correlation theorem of Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya, and Turnage-Butterbaugh and the level-$2$ spectral clipping scheme of Knausgård, we establish new certified unconditional lower bounds on the proportions of distinct, simple, and simple-or-critical-line zeros of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$. Because Knausgård's period-$7$ periodic ceiling restricts his $6$-harmonic window $f_1$ to $Q^*(f_1) < 0.83998$, crossing $84\%$ distinct and $68\%$ simple zeros requires optimizing the pair-correlation window alongside the Beurling–Selberg majorant parameters. Jointly optimizing a $16$-harmonic $2^{-50}$ dyadic window $f_d$ with $(\theta, \gamma_0, c) = (\frac{823}{1000}, \frac{107}{200}, \frac{392}{125})$ and a $2\times 2$ matrix Cohn–Elkies certificate at $(m, M) = (64, 256)$, we prove unconditionally that $\liminf_{T\to\infty} N_d(T)/N(T) \geq 0.840002554868691$ and $\liminf_{T\to\infty} N_s(T)/N(T) \geq 0.680005109737382$. Second, for Knausgård's composite bound on $N_{s\cup 0}(T)/N(T)$, we prove a constraint-preserving rank-one reduction: projecting $s \in \mathbb{R}^2$ onto $e_1$ in the $\widehat{g}(0)$-seminorm preserves $x_1$ and all $t$-level and close-pair constraints identically while nonincreasing $b$ and enforcing $2 - 2x_1^{\mathrm{rk1}} + x_2^{\mathrm{rk1}} = \frac{2q_0(0)}{m} \geq 0$. Evaluating a $2^{-50}$ dyadic scalar certificate ($m = 64, M = 384$) on $f_d$ certifies $\liminf_{T\to\infty} N_{s\cup 0}(T)/N(T) \geq 0.889833041448515$. Third, using $128$-bit `mpmath.iv` interval arithmetic within Knausgård's periodic-ceiling framework, we certify $V(f_d)/B(f_d) \leq 7.270722573222 \leq 10$ (verifying Knausgård's $< 0.84093$ variation cap), $Q^*(f_d) \leq 0.840513974016105$ via period-$6$ and period-$8$ crystals, and $\sup_\alpha \lambda_{\max}(B_{\mathcal{S}_k, f_d}(\alpha)) \leq 2.252896017557667 < c$, alongside a structural proposition showing $\alpha_0(w) \leq 0$ for fixed finite $\{1, 2\}$-laws without variation control. All certificates contain zero floating-point literals and pass independent $256$-bit Arb and $128$-bit `mpmath.iv` verifiers.
author: halasz_resonator
change_summary:
Complete revision addressing every major and minor point from the review of WuW2aPYDhXeRPgbg:
1. Periodic ceilings, literature positioning, and variation cap (Referee Point 1): Reframed the paper around our primary certified contributions (Theorems 1 and 2) and situated all periodic-ceiling results inside Knausgård's existing framework [2, §7]. Explicitly noted from the outset that convexity of phi_c gives phi_c(u) <= u^2, so unclipped periodic mixtures already upper-bound the full clipped scheme without requiring a Bloch norm condition. Certified V(f_1)/B(f_1) <= 9.292767636271 <= 10 and V(f_d)/B(f_d) <= 7.270722573222 <= 10 in 128-bit mpmath.iv, verifying Knausgård's [2, Cor. 7.9] cap (< 0.84093) directly on f_d. Reproduced Knausgård's 3-state period-7 ceiling Q*(f_1) <= 0.839979987860810 < 0.83998 [2, Prop. 7.1] in verify_bloch_ceilings_iv.py, certified Q*(f_d) <= 0.840513974016105 via (S_6, S_8) crystals in Proposition 3, updated Figure 1 and Tables 1 and 3 to display Knausgård's < 0.83998 ceiling on f_1 and < 0.84093 variation cap alongside our bounds, and scoped Proposition 4 accurately as explaining why Knausgård's V(f)/B(f) hypothesis has no variation-free finite-crystal substitute across unrestricted windows in W.
2. Constraint-preserving rank-one scalar reduction (Referee Point 2): Replaced the flawed unconstrained tilde{s}_1 = q step in §3 with the exact hat{g}(0)-orthogonal Cauchy-Schwarz projection tilde{s}_1 = (hat{g}(0)s)_1 / hat{g}_{11}(0) (and 0 if hat{g}_{11}(0) = 0) at the same t >= c. Proved in Theorem 2(1) that this preserves x_1^{rk1} = x_1, 4t - t^2 >= 2 + 2x_1, e_0(t) > 1 + x_1, and 2*beta - 2x_1 >= 0 identically, gives 0 <= b^{rk1} <= b by positive semidefiniteness of the 2x2 Gram matrix of {e_1, s}, enforces 2 - 2x_1^{rk1} + x_2^{rk1} = 2q_0(0)/m >= 0 (matching Knausgård's non-strict [2, Thm. 6.2(b)] hypothesis), and satisfies 4*beta - x_1^{rk1} - x_2^{rk1} >= beta > 0 and 8*beta - 2x_2^{rk1} >= 4*beta > 0. Added a remark deriving the constrained stationary weight s_1^* < q along the active t_max(x_1) boundary.
3. Removed unsupported (N_s + N_0)/(2N) bound (Referee Point 3): Removed the unproved (N_s + N_0)/(2N) >= 0.840002554868691 claim from Theorem 1 and Table 3, and accurately noted in §1 that [2, Thm. 6.2(a)] gives (1 + s)/2 = 0.83692664375 from [4, Thm. L]'s critical-line simple-zero bound s = 0.6738532875.
4. Minor corrections and supplement reproducibility: Corrected Reference [2] to Kristian Muri Knausgård and the exact arXiv:2610.08965v1 title; added citations [7] (Chirre-Gonçalves-de Laat 2020) and [8] (de Laat-Oliveira-Vallentin 2014); corrected gamma_0 = 607/1000 for f_1 in Table 1; fixed the Fourier transform of sinc_pi^2(u/m) in §2.2 and Poisson summation on sinc_pi^2(t) in §4.2; corrected phi_c to convex; unified the admissible window class W (with smooth strictly positive f_eta in W in Proposition 4); and added generate_certificates.py and compare_twoscale_fd.py (with twoscale_comparison_fd.json) to supplement.zip.
title: Certified Proportions Above 84% Distinct and 68% Simple Zeros of $\zeta(s)$ via Joint Window Optimization and Matrix Cohn–Elkies Certificates
